claims.text: FeCoNiCrAl feedstock with a particle size of 15–45 μm previously yielded high-quality coatings.
The 15–45 μm feedstock previously produced minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
Baseline HVAF-i7 deposition of 15–45 μm FeCoNiCrAl feedstock produces acceptable coating quality.
Baseline HVAF-i7 deposition produces insufficient coating thickness.
Increasing the HVAF-i7 nozzle-to-substrate distance to approximately 300–350 mm will increase particle velocity.
Increasing the HVAF-i7 nozzle-to-substrate distance to approximately 300–350 mm will increase deposition efficiency.
Higher particle velocity promotes stronger inter-particle bonding.
Particles gain greater momentum and kinetic energy when spray distance is increased.
Greater particle kinetic energy causes more effective peening and mechanical interlocking on impact.
Enhanced peening and interlocking will build a thicker coating.
A spray distance of 300–350 mm will produce a thicker FeCoNiCrAl coating than the baseline spray distance.
The thicker coating produced at 300–350 mm will remain adherent.
The coating produced at 300–350 mm will retain minimal oxidation.
The coating produced at 300–350 mm will maintain performance during high-temperature service and thermal cycling.
The proposed 300–350 mm spray distance is expected to remain effective for internal geometries around 120 mm in diameter.
Changes in feedstock characteristics or substrate geometry may alter the intervention's outcome.

contradictions.description: A nozzle-to-substrate distance of 300–350 mm is not geometrically compatible with deposition inside a 120 mm internal diameter under an ordinary radial spray arrangement. The hypothesis does not specify specialized axial tooling or another geometry that would reconcile these requirements.
The conditions require effectiveness in approximately 120 mm internal geometries, but the proposed experiment only specifies identical substrates and does not test an internal-diameter geometry.
